prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for every homeowner — the right contractor depends on your exact location in Atlanta, your budget, the type/size of system you need, and whether you prefer a big franchise or a local company. I can help you find the best option for your situation — but first, here are the practical things to look for and steps to take so you pick the right company.

How to choose the best contractor
- Get multiple bids (3 recommended) so you can compare price, equipment, and scope.
- Require a Manual J load calculation. Any reputable contractor should size the system to your home (not just “rule of thumb”).
- Check credentials: licensed, insured, and (if available) NATE-certified technicians.
- Read recent reviews on Google, Yelp, and the BBB; look for consistent themes (quality, timeliness, follow-up).
- Ask about brands they install and why; prefer companies that install ENERGY STAR–rated equipment and provide performance data.
- Confirm warranty details: manufacturer warranty + labor/service warranty and what each covers.
- Ask about permits, rebates, and energy-efficiency incentives; good contractors pull permits and help with rebates.
- Ask about financing, maintenance plans, and response time for service calls.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Can you do a Manual J load calculation and show me the results?
- What exact model (SEER/HSPF) are you recommending and why?
- What’s included in the install price? (ductwork, permits, disconnects, cleanup, thermostat, refrigerant charge)
- What warranties apply (parts, labor, compressor) and are any extended warranties available?
- Are your technicians certified/licensed and insured? Can you provide references?
- How long will the job take and what’s your service/repair response time?

Red flags
- No written estimate or evasive about load calculations.
- Very low price compared to others with vague scope.
- Pressure to buy immediately without answering technical questions.
- Poor or no local references or a history of unresolved BBB complaints.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies in your Atlanta ZIP code and compare reviews/specifications for you (share your ZIP), or
- Recommend what equipment (heat pump vs. AC, SEER level) is likely best based on your home size/age if you tell me square footage, number of stories, attic/insulation condition, and whether you have ductwork.

Which would you prefer?
